answer_summary: F is the unsilylated first 1,4-diol; G is its bis-OTES ether; H is the terminal phenol after OTBS cleavage; I is the corresponding para-hydroxycyclohexadienone; J is the second 1,4-diol after para-bromophenyllithium addition; K is its bis-OTES ether; L is the five-unit macrocycle formed by intramolecular coupling of the two terminal aryl bromides.
assumptions: Standard organolithium addition to a cyclohexadienone carbonyl followed by work-up gives the corresponding alcohol and installs the aryl group.
TESCl/imidazole protects the two free masked-ring alcohols as OTES ethers.
In the stated sequence LiOH selectively exposes the terminal phenol from its OTBS ether while retaining the two masked-ring OTES groups.
Aqueous PhI(OAc)2 performs two-electron oxidative dearomatization of the para-substituted phenol to the para-hydroxycyclohexadienone.
Ni(COD)2/2,2'-bipyridine replaces the two terminal aryl C-Br bonds by the intramolecular aryl-aryl C-C bond.
The absence of stereochemical marks in the source and blank answer sheets means configurations are unspecified rather than assigned.
